title: State of Startups and AI 2025 - Sarah Guo, Conviction
talk_summary: Sarah Guo's VC keynote surveys 2025 AI capability trends (reasoning, multimodality, agents) and argues the durable value is in thick workflow products that package context and orchestrate multiple models, not thin wrappers.

takeaways.what_they_do: Cursor uses different models for different sub-tasks (diffs, merges, embeddings) and routes each to the right model rather than one model for everything.

takeaways.technique: Package context automatically, prompt is a bug
takeaways.what_they_do: Winning products collect and package context from multiple sources automatically so users don't hand-write prompts; the prompt is treated as a stepping stone, not the interface.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They collect and package context automatically including from other sources not just natural language presented to the models

takeaways.what_they_do: Argues human tolerance for agent failure drops as latency rises, so build strong augmentation (copilot) and extend autonomy incrementally rather than jumping to full automation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: human tolerance for failure or hallucinations or lack of reliability, it just reduces dramatically as latency increases

takeaways.technique: Deterministic validation as the moat for code agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Explains code was first because it has deterministic validation — tests, compile, execute — letting you automatically check if output works.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have deterministic validation. You can automatically check if code works, run tests, compile, execute

takeaways.what_they_do: Notes rapid price collapse (GPT-4 $30→$2/M tokens in ~18 months, distilled ~10c) and advises planning for a multimodel world via routers/inference platforms.
takeaways.evidence_quote: GPT4 went from $30 per million tokens to $2 in about 18 months. The distilled versions of that are like now 10 cents.
takeaways.numbers: GPT-4 $30→$2 per M tokens in ~18 months; distilled ~$0.10/M
